System Backup & Restore

Back up and restore SATOM itself — database bundles, device-config versions, code rollback, git repository bundles and the external backup server — from one admin page.

👤 ForAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsusers.manage
📍 WhereSettings → Source of Truth & Backup → System Backup & Restore (URL /system-backup/)

What is it?#

System Backup & Restore is the page that protects SATOM itself — not the appliances. From it you take and restore whole-instance database bundles, see every backup stream at a glance, browse the device-config versions SATOM has recorded, roll the application code back to an earlier commit, and reach the external backup server where appliances push their own configuration archives and where firmware images are kept.

Per-appliance configuration backups (the device vault) are a different feature: see Device backups.

What does it do?#

  • Backup coverage — everything, at a glance. One table listing every backup stream (application code, live database, database bundles, device-config source of truth, git repository, device-config vault, appliance-pushed configs, firmware) with its format, where it lives, how often it is taken and a live state badge.
  • Database bundles. Create backup now writes a single .tar.gz containing a pg_dump of the database plus, optionally, the per-device JSON tree and the versioned source-of-truth store, and can push it to the backup server. Bundles can be downloaded, restored or deleted.
  • Restore. Replaces the current database (and the per-device JSON tree and source-of-truth store) with a bundle, taking a safety bundle first.
  • Device config versions. Records the current per-device JSON into the versioned source-of-truth store on demand, pushes new versions to the backup server, and compares any two recorded versions of a device.
  • Application code rollback. Lists the last 15 commits and queues a rollback to one of them through the Software Update runner.
  • External backup server. Lists the configuration archives each appliance pushed to the SFTP backup server, lets you compare, search, read and download them, and pulls archived firmware images into the local firmware store.
  • Git repository bundles. Packs the whole application repository (every commit, branch and tag) into one verifiable file, keeps a configurable number per node, optionally pushes it to the backup server, and lets you download it back from there.
  • Peer comparison. When a second node is registered for High Availability, shows which database bundles exist on this node and on the peer, and flags size differences.

Requirements#

  • A user with the users.manage permission, working in the Global ADOM (the Administrator menu that carries this page is part of the Global navigation).
  • The PostgreSQL client tools (pg_dump, pg_restore) on the node — bundles are created and restored by running them.
  • For anything "off-box" (bundle upload, device-pushed archives, firmware archive, git bundle push): the external backup server configured in Settings → Backup Server. Without it the related cards say Not configured — set host / credentials in Settings → Backup Server.
  • For the peer comparison card: a peer registered on the High Availability page.

Permissions#

Every route on this page — viewing, creating, downloading, restoring, deleting, rolling back code, browsing the backup server — requires users.manage (legacy coarse key user_manage; in the default profiles only Administrator has it).

🔑Permission

Users without users.manage do not see the Administrator menu at all, and opening /system-backup/ directly returns 403 Forbidden.

Two actions are additionally restricted by node role:

  • Delete (database bundles and git bundles) is refused on a standby node, because the standby's data/ directory is re-synced from the primary and the deletion would be undone.
  • Code rollback affects only the node you run it on; repeat it on the other node of a pair. On a primary with registered peers it obeys the same staged-rollout safeguard as Software Update: the standby must run the target commit and pass its health check first.
  • On a container installation, code rollback is refused with the reason (code is changed by replacing the image there).

How to use#

Create a database bundle#

  1. Open Settings → Source of Truth & Backup → System Backup & Restore.
  2. In the Create backup card, leave Include per-device JSON (reports/) ticked to include the per-device JSON tree and the versioned source-of-truth store, or clear it for a database-only bundle.
  3. When a backup server is configured, the card also offers Also push the bundle to the backup server (off-box copy), ticked by default. Leave it ticked for an off-box copy, or clear it to keep the bundle on this node only.
  4. Click Create backup now.
  5. The flash message reads Backup created: fmw-backup-<timestamp>.tar.gz (<size> KB) — <details>. The details list what went in, for example db.dump=…B; reports/ included; sot/ included; recovery-seal included.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: Create backup now can push the bundle to the backup server (before, a manual bundle never left the node), code rollback obeys the staged-rollout safeguard and is refused with a reason on a container installation, and every action on this page is audited.

Download a bundle#

In Database backups — pg_dump bundles (this node), click the download icon on a row. Keeping a downloaded copy is the one copy that is guaranteed to live somewhere other than the SATOM nodes.

Restore a bundle#

⚠️Warning

Restore is destructive: it replaces the current database, the per-device JSON tree and the versioned source-of-truth store with the bundle's content. Run it on the primary — a standby's database is read-only.

  1. In Database backups — pg_dump bundles (this node), click Restore on the bundle you want.
  2. The Restore database dialog names the bundle. Type RESTORE in the box.
  3. Click Restore.
  4. SATOM first creates a safety bundle of the current state, then restores. The flash reads Restored <bundle>. Safety dump: <safety bundle>. <details>.

If the bundle was taken under a different encryption key, the details start with a warning (see Troubleshooting).

Delete old bundles#

  1. Click Manage / clean up in the database bundles card header.
  2. In Database bundles on this node, click the trash icon on a row; the button changes to Sure? click again for four seconds — click it again to delete.
  3. Do this on the primary: the deletion reaches the standby with the next data sync (every 5 minutes).

Record device config versions and push them off-box#

Click Record versions + push off-box now (in the Create backup card). Every per-device _config.json is recorded into the versioned store (an unchanged config adds nothing) and new blobs are uploaded to the backup server. The flash reads SoT recorded: N device(s), M new version(s). Off-box: …. The hourly device sync records versions automatically; this button is for an immediate copy.

Compare two device config versions#

  1. In Device config versions (SoT store) — compare / rollback, pick one row in column A and one in column B (by default the two newest are selected).
  2. Click Compare A → B.
  3. The result shows added, removed and changed objects with field-level detail, or Versions #A and #B are identical.

Pick two versions of the same device. This view is read-only: it does not push anything to a device.

Roll back the application code#

  1. In Application code — versions & rollback, click the rollback icon on the commit you want (the running commit is marked running and has no button).
  2. The Roll back application code dialog names the commit and its subject. Type ROLLBACK.
  3. Click Queue rollback. The flash reads Code rollback to <commit> queued (<id>) — follow it on the Software Update page. The service restarts when it applies. On a primary with registered peers, roll the standby back first; until it runs that commit and passes its health check, the primary refuses with Blocked by the staged-rollout safeguard: ….
  4. Follow the steps on Software Update.

❗Important

A code rollback does not downgrade the database schema. If the newer code introduced a migration, pair the code rollback with a database bundle restore.

Browse device-pushed backups on the external backup server#

  1. In External backup server, click Browse on a device row.
  2. The dialog lists every archive the appliance pushed. Pick A and B.
  3. Use Compare A → B, type a term and press the search button (search in B…), What's inside B (sections, with encrypted or binary ones listed separately), View B (or click a file name) to read the extracted configuration text, or Download B for the raw archive.

These archives are written by the appliances themselves on their own schedule; SATOM only reads them.

Pull a firmware image#

In Firmware on the backup server, click Pull on an image. It is copied into Infrastructure → Firmware (sha256-verified), where the per-appliance Upgrade / Downgrade actions can use it. Images already present show in console instead. See Firmware.

Create and manage git repository bundles#

  1. In Git repository backup — bundles, tick Also push to the external backup server (separate failure domain) if you want an off-box copy.
  2. Click Create repository bundle now.
  3. Each bundle row shows size, head commit, number of refs and its sha256. Use the download icon to save it, or the trash icon (two clicks) to delete it on the primary.
  4. Check backup server lists the bundles held on the backup server, each with a download link — the recovery direction when this node is the one that was lost.

To restore from a bundle: git clone <bundle> satom, or into an existing checkout git fetch <bundle> '+refs/*:refs/recovered/*'. Verify it first with sha256sum against the value shown on the page.

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Include per-device JSON (reports/) Adds the per-device JSON tree and the versioned source-of-truth store to a manual bundle. Ticked by default. No ticked
Also push the bundle to the backup server (off-box copy) Uploads the manual bundle to the backup server. Shown only when a backup server is configured; ticked by default. No ticked
Restore confirmation Must be exactly RESTORE. Yes (restore) RESTORE
Rollback confirmation Must be exactly ROLLBACK. Yes (code rollback) ROLLBACK
Bundles to keep on each node Number of git repository bundles retained per node, 1–50. Default 7. No 7
Push to the backup server by default (scheduled runs too) Default for the git-bundle push option. On by default. No ticked

Related settings that live elsewhere:

  • Nightly database bundle — the scheduled action system_backup (System backup (Postgres + JSON)), default time 01:30 node wall-clock. Its push_server parameter (default on) uploads the bundle to the backup server. See Scheduled actions.
  • Local bundle retention after upload — how many database bundles stay on the node once the backup server verifiably holds them (default 0), and the backup server connection itself: Settings → Backup Server.

Example#

🧪Example — Nightly bundle plus a pre-change manual bundle

Before a risky maintenance window, an administrator opens System Backup & Restore, leaves Include per-device JSON ticked and clicks Create backup now. The flash reports fmw-backup-20261003-081500.tar.gz with reports/ included; sot/ included; recovery-seal included. She downloads it to her workstation. The maintenance goes wrong; she clicks Restore on that bundle, types RESTORE, and SATOM first writes a safety bundle of the broken state, then restores the morning's database.

Result#

  • A database bundle is a file named fmw-backup-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.tar.gz (UTC timestamp) in the node's data/system_backups/ directory, mode 0600 in a 0700 directory: only the service account can read it. On a pair, the standby receives a copy with the next data sync.
  • A restore leaves an additional safety bundle (manifest label pre-restore-safety).
  • A code rollback appears in Recent updates on the Software Update page.

  • Git bundles are named satom-repo-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.bundle in data/git-bundles/.

  • Creating, restoring and deleting a database bundle, creating and deleting a git bundle, saving the git-bundle settings, pulling a firmware image and queuing a code rollback each write an Audit Log entry (a rollback refused by the staged-rollout safeguard is audited too, as system.code_rollback with refused).

Troubleshooting#

"Restore not confirmed — type RESTORE to proceed."#

Possible causes - The confirmation box was empty or not exactly RESTORE (upper case).

Solution 1. Click Restore again and type RESTORE.

Verification - The flash starts with Restored ….

"Backup failed: pg_dump failed: …"#

Possible causes - pg_dump is not installed or cannot reach the database. - The database credentials in the application configuration are wrong.

Solution 1. Read the error text after pg_dump failed: — it is the tool's own message. 2. Fix the connection or install the PostgreSQL client tools, then retry.

Verification - Backup created: … and a new row in the bundles table.

Restore message warns about a different FERNET_KEY#

Possible causes - The bundle was taken on a node with a different FERNET_KEY, or this node has none. The message begins This bundle was taken under a DIFFERENT FERNET_KEY … or This node has no FERNET_KEY, so the restored encrypted columns cannot be read.

Solution 1. Put the matching key into the node's .env and restart the service before relying on any stored credential. 2. Bundles deliberately do not contain the key. Run satom diagnose recovery to check that someone holds it.

Verification - Appliance connections that use stored credentials work again.

"This node is the standby — delete bundles on the primary; the datasync mirrors the deletion here within 5 minutes."#

Possible causes - You tried to delete a database or git bundle on the standby.

Solution 1. Open this page on the primary and delete it there.

Verification - Within 5 minutes the bundle is gone from the standby too.

"Rollback not confirmed — type ROLLBACK to proceed." / "Pick a commit to roll back to."#

Solution 1. Click the rollback icon on a commit row, then type ROLLBACK exactly.

If the flash says Already running that revision., the selected commit is the one already running.

"Blocked by the staged-rollout safeguard: roll the STANDBY back to this revision and let it pass its health check first, then the PRIMARY unlocks."#

Possible causes - You queued a code rollback on the primary of a pair, and the standby does not run that commit yet (or has not passed its health check on it).

Solution 1. Open this page on the standby and roll it back to the same commit. 2. When the standby is healthy on it, repeat the rollback on the primary.

Verification - The primary's flash reads Code rollback to … queued ….

"Peer <host> unreachable — off-box bundle copy cannot be verified right now."#

Possible causes - The registered peer is down or does not answer on its health endpoint.

Solution 1. Check the peer on High Availability.

Verification - The Backup server (standby) card shows a per-bundle comparison table.

A bundle reported on the backup server is missing from the table#

Possible causes - After a verified upload, the nightly run removes local copies the backup server holds byte-for-byte (default: keep none). The Database backups table lists only bundles physically on this node; the coverage table shows how many the backup server holds and names the newest one.

Solution 1. Opening /system-backup/download/<bundle name> fetches an evicted bundle back from the backup server (size-checked) before sending it. 2. To keep some bundles locally, raise the local retention in Settings → Backup Server.

satom diagnose data reports bundles or vault entries "too open"#

Possible causes — the node was installed by a release that left data/ 0755 and its files 0644, and has not had the repair applied yet.

Solution — on the node, run sudo satom execute repair data to see the plan, then sudo satom execute repair data --yes to apply it. It only removes permission bits and never follows a link.

Verification — sudo satom diagnose data reports readable by other accounts: none.

"Firmware pull failed: …"#

Possible causes - The file is not a .out image (only .out firmware images can be pulled). - The backup server is unreachable.

Solution 1. Check the External backup server card for an unreachable message and the backup server settings.

Advanced#

Advanced What a database bundle contains
  • db.dump — pg_dump -Fc of the whole database.
  • reports/ and sot/ — the per-device JSON tree and the content-addressed source-of-truth store (when Include per-device JSON is ticked). The database only holds the version index; the blobs must travel with it.
  • recovery-seal.json — the sealed recovery envelope, if this node has one. It is ciphertext; the detail reports recovery-seal ABSENT (no off-node custody) when there is none.
  • config/ — the node's publication overlay, if present.
  • manifest.txt — label, timestamp, database name and host, and key fingerprints (never the keys).
Advanced How a restore runs
  1. If the bundle is not on disk, it is fetched back from the backup server first (downloaded to a temporary name and renamed only when the size matches).
  2. A safety bundle is created.
  3. The bundle is extracted into a private (0700) work directory and key fingerprints are compared. Because a bundle may come back from the off-box server, it is read as untrusted: only regular files and directories are extracted (symbolic links, hard links and device entries are skipped), a member is kept only if its resolved path is inside the work directory (a real path check, not a name-prefix comparison), and Python's data extraction filter is applied where the interpreter provides it.
  4. pg_restore --clean --if-exists --no-owner runs. A non-zero exit code is accepted when its output contains no "error" (benign DROP warnings).
  5. reports/ and the source-of-truth store are replaced. The recovery seal and config/ files are placed only if the node has none — a live node's own copies are newer by definition.
Advanced Who can read bundles and device configurations
  • data/ is 0750 and owned by the service account, whose group has no other members. The bundle store (data/system_backups/) and the device config vault (data/backups/) hold 0700 directories and 0600 files.
  • A bundle is created 0600 from its first byte (written through a private file descriptor that refuses a symbolic link, never narrowed afterwards); a bundle fetched back from the backup server is written the same way. The service umask stays 0022 on purpose; the directory modes do the work.
  • satom diagnose data reports anything looser and sudo satom execute repair data --yes narrows it (see CLI). On a node installed before this protection, the update that brings it closes the vault and bundle directories the next time the application writes to them; the update runner repairs the whole of data/ from the following update on. Run the repair by hand to close it at once.
Advanced Off-box copies and eviction
  • The scheduled system_backup action uploads each new bundle to <system path>/ on the backup server. After a successful, size-verified upload, local bundles are deleted only if the server holds the same name at the same size; the newest keep bundles are always kept. An unreachable server is treated as "nothing is off-box" and deletes nothing.
  • The peer comparison card asks the peer's unauthenticated /healthz/backups endpoint through the peer's node vhost on port 8443 (bundle names, sizes, dates and vault entry count only — no content). It reports what each node physically holds.
  • The "git publish" option of older releases is accepted but does nothing: the device-config history moved to the local versioned store.

  • "This node is the standby — delete bundles on the primary; the datasync mirrors the deletion here within 5 minutes."
  • "Rollback not confirmed — type ROLLBACK to proceed." / "Pick a commit to roll back to."
  • "Blocked by the staged-rollout safeguard: roll the STANDBY back to this revision and let it pass its health check first, then the PRIMARY unlocks."
  • "Peer <host> unreachable — off-box bundle copy cannot be verified right now."
  • A bundle reported on the backup server is missing from the table
  • satom diagnose data reports bundles or vault entries "too open"
  • "Firmware pull failed: …"
